rows.t:
Currently a work in progress. Feedback is welcome.

Last Updated 9/13/2026

Will explain what makes a comp different from release, and what has been added or changed.

Type of comp: Remaster, Vanilla, overhaul, renovation, extension, remix, shitpost, and playlist.

Era refers to an album, or period of time that the comp is based on or taking place during.

A comps cover will be displayed in this column when applicable.

Kanye West would begin work in the music industry producing beats, and recording with a Chicago based rap group featuring GLC, Timmy G, and Arrowstar while trying to find his sound. Although Kanye's signature sample chopping is present for many of these tracks that were released on mixtapes or leaked, he would later state he was dissatisfied with the persona he put on and would course correct to a more authentic one going forward. Although there were tracks he made and worked on during these years this section is meant for this specific rap group. The era currently only has one comp but future comps would need to be based on the tracks produced with the Go-Getters members and Kanye to fit into this slot.

World Record Holders compiles and remasters the tracks produced by the Go-Getters in the vein of old school hip-hop with Kanye's iconic sample choping on display. Goose's contributions include new production, remixed and/or re-arranged verses, and mixing to make the overall quality of the comp consistent. Goose has stated he would like to remaster/remake this comp himself. - 100greenmen

gv's personal remaster of Goose's World Record Holders comp and based on Big Brother's earth 2054 timeline. The track 16. "His Name Means Love (Outro)" was omitted entirely from Goose's comp. - 100greenmen

Kanye West's first studio album released in 2003. After many attempts to find a label that would release his music, this album faced numerous delays and changes in direction (most notably a nearly fatal car crash), ultimately steering away from the usual sounds of hip hop, focusing on a unique style of sampling for the time, lyrics that reflected Kanye's beliefs and anxieties, in the hopes that he could inspire other people with his poetic prose and optimistic outlook on breaking away from established norms. Comps from this era contain a large number of scrapped tracks dating back to Kanye's solo work in the late 90's, and tracks after he signed with Roc-A-Fella, as well as released tracks.

FosterLynch's extensive remaster of college dropout scraps, and other Kanye tracks sourced from various mixtapes released between 1999 and 2002. The Lo-Fi quality is preserved while mixing is updated for modern audio devices. - 100greenmen

FosterLynch's remaster of the college dropout's release tracks, as well as an alternate version of we don't care and a few scrapped tracks. Updated for modern audio devices. May be out of date, however the audio quality and mixing on offer is superior to any given version available on streaming services. - 100greenmen

SimpleJosh's take on a Kanye West Mixtape after he started producing music with Roc-a-fella records, fairly faithful remasters to the tracks from their respective mixtapes. Contains two versions of Drop Dead Gorgeous as bonus tracks, and a few early versions of college dropout songs. - 100greenmen

A short selection of tracks, and a custom intro track made before and during The College Dropout era with cleaned up audio, presumably chosen for their consistent old school hip hop sound. A good companion album to listen to alongside the college dropout itself. - 100greenmen

An extension adding new audio bytes, interviews, and samples as intros and outtros to some songs, while others are identical to the official release. Some scrapped or alt takes were added as additional verses to the extended songs, while still maintaining the official college dropout tracklist. - 100greenmen

One of the most famous fan compilation and bootlegs of all time. A label seemingly created for the distribution of this and a few other bootlegs compiles early versions of tracks from the College Dropout and other leaked tracks from Kanye’s time at Roc-A-Fella records. It was initially distributed on CD and Vinyl in 2005 up until the label quietly shut down in 2007. – 100greenmen

A comp that merges skits with songs, extends them with alt/scrapped verses, ad-libs, and adds a few tracks produced during Kanye's time working under Roc-a-fella. Notably does not change last call. - 100greenmen

Mostly uses edits from SimpleJosh's dream killers, this playlist is gv's personal take on the college dropout based on Big Brother's earth 2054 timeline with a fair number of songs from the official tracklist for college dropout and scraps. Meant to be an earlier iteration of what would become the college dropout based on leaks and mixtapes before 2004. - 100greenmen
Credits list, one bonus track, explanation by gv

Slightly tweaked version of the college dropout, some songs come with a mix of minor added production, new mixes, new samples, scrapped verses added back, etc. Some scrapped songs are added back, skits are merged with some songs. Cover uses an ai upscaled photo, likely using an emerging free model from 2022, or possibly earlier. - 100greenmen
A selection of early tracks, leaked and released on mixtapes meant to be a fabrication of an early solo Kanye album. – 100greenmen
Skits are merged with songs, scrapped verses are added back to some songs, new mixing noteably boosts the vocals. - 100greenmen

Likely the editors first comp, it is a vaporwave conversion of TCD material. Beats are slowed, pitched down and extended with lyrics from various pop songs added alongside new samples, while other songs are cut short in this style to serve as interludes. Only one is added despite no relation to TCD. – 100greenmen

The first comp from Xenniversary for his personal timeline. It includes almost every song Kanye made leading up to the College dropout from mixtapes, leaks, etc. Contains some unique transitions, new intros and outtros, and extended samples from the sources. - 100greenmen

Remade from the ground up for the editors personal timeline, this comp follows the same path as the previous iteration with a trimmed down tracklist, while still having lengthy tracks. Contains new custom intros and outtros, even a few skits pulled from various sources. – 100greenmen

A comp aiming to imagine an early version of the college dropout, includes many songs from before Kanye signed with Roc-a-fella, adds a new interlude, new production and mixing emphasizing the bass. - 100greenmen

A bootleg that contains recordings of a live performance by Kanye in Amsterdam. Mostly songs from The College Dropout with some unreleased songs included as bonus tracks, an early performance of Hey Mama was also part of the performance. Printed on CD by a label likely created just to produce this bootleg. – 100greenmen

Kanye West's second studio album, Late Registration released in 2005. After the success of The College Dropout, work on this record would begin with old and new songs as a victory lap to celebrate his breakout success. Numerous delays changed the direction from sounding identical to The College Dropout to a focus on imitating a movie soundtrack. The themes of conscious hip-hop continue here as his poetic writing style matures. Late Orchestration was a live performance that included a full orchestra accompanying Kanye's live performances containing songs from Late Registration, and The College Dropout. Comps from this era contain released and scrapped songs worked on during this period, as well as some tracks from The College Dropout.
This comp remasters the audio for the eponymous Late Orchestration Live album. Removes or reduces crowd noise, sounds more like a studio recorded album. - 100greenmen
New instrumental additions to this ep length comp give the tracks a fresh take on the live recordings, with some updated mixing as well. - 100greenmen

gv's personal take on big brother's earth 2054 timeline version of Late Registration. Utilizing edits from a few different comps of this era with solo edits and further altering or re-arranging them. Some songs are carried over from the college dropout era and suited to fit the sound of this particular comp, while others are songs from Common's Album Be. - 100greenmen
One alt track, credits and explanation by gv

A significant update to gv’s playlist with updated mixing and remade edits. Additional vocals also fill in more of some of the tracks. A few unique transitions for some tracks differentiate it from the previous iteration. – 100greenmen

Mixing has been adjusted to emphasize the instrumentals, new orchestral production added on some tracks, skits merged with tracks. An edit of bittersweet poetry is included, in the spirit of it's original intended inclusion with the album. - 100greenmen

This is the furthest I’m willing to stretch the definition of a comp to include for my archive. Officially produced by Kanye’s tour DJ for Japan at the request of Tube Records with some help from Kanye himself. It features extended samples used by Kanye and his collaborators during his early years extended and adjusted to sound how they did in the actual tracks. Occasional narration and comments by Kanye are also on most tracks. – 100greenmen
The Good, The Bad, & The Ugly

An alternative take on the era that depicts a collaboration between Kanye, Common, and Consequence. Songs are taken from a variety of projects from the time Late Registration was released, and adds features from the other artists to the others respective songs despite some quirks with the vocal stems used. Includes new production as well. An alternative version of the comp is available without the additional features and verses. - 100greenmen
Five bonus tracks, alt with fewer added verses/features is avaliable.
Extended intros and outtros are added to various songs, also includes the track back to basics. - 100greenmen

A comp with a reduced tracklist completed for Yedits 2026 one-week-comp competition, it uses some live vocals from Late Orchestration, remastered by Bobert with with the intent of re-creating the CD release of Late Orchestration in a higher quality. Minor production elements are added as well. - 100greenmen

An expanded and further enhanced rendition of the one-week-comp bobert previously made. Tracks from the previous comp have been updated slightly while the rest of the new additions have had futher tweaks, be it added verses, adjusted mixing, or further edits in the same style as the previous version. - 100greenmen
An extension adding back scrapped/alt verses, skits are merged with songs and some songs are combined as well. Extended intros and outtros. - 100greenmen

The sequel to Freshman Adjustment, this time with leaks and early versions of tracks from Late Registration, although a good portion of songs are lifted from TCD and various tracks by Consequence that Kanye produced. This volume was printed and distributed from 2006 until the label shut down in 2007. - 100greenmen

The final installment in the Freshman Adjustment bootlegs. More leaked and released tracks from Kanye’s collaborators are included, as well as recordings of live Kanye Performances. Half of the tracks are remixes of songs from TCD and LR. It was distributed in 2007 until the label shut down making it the hardest of the series to come by. - 100greenmen

Despite the name, this comp contains a fair bit of material ranging from LR and even GAJ. Intended as a pseudo sequel to Late Registration proper, it has a lot of instrumentals and features from some of Kanye's collaborators from the time period. A lot of new production and samples are also added accurately reflecting his production style from 2006. – 100greenmen
Multiple file formats, 2 bonus tracks, 3 alt tracks.
FosterLynch's remaster of Late Registration, includes Back to basics and We can make it better. Overall higher quality audio than what most streaming services have on offer. - 100greenmen

A sequel to Neo-CSU.Dropout, converting LR material to vaporwave tracks with pop song lyrics replacing most of Kanye’s. New production and samples litter the pitched down and extended tracks. A few songs are taken from other eras for no apparent reason. – 100greenmen.

Kanye West's third studio album graduation released in 2007. The movie soundtrack inspired hip-hop Kanye Had produced for Late registration is expanded upon in this record ultimately resulting in a love letter to pop culture, that went on to define pop culture for the rest of the decade. Lyrically it focuses on emotional introspection and expression of the ego. Different regions had remixes of some songs as bonus tracks, and The track Bittersweet Poetry was included in the Japanese release of the album as a bonus. The track Good Night was included on streaming services as a bonus. Comps from this era contain the release tracks, tracks he produced for during the late 2000's and a few choice tracks from Late Registration.
An extension of graduation adding back scrapped or alt verses, new instrumental intros and outtros, and extended samples from their source. Also includes bittersweet poetry. - 100greenmen
Renovation, JuyTuy, Multiple file formats, 2 alt covers, 1 scrapped track.

An ep-length comp featuring a few kanye produced tracks. Unique harmonies, beat re-creations as well as added production on every track make for a condensed, but enhanced listening experience – 100greenmen

A collaborative project aiming to make the definitive Graduation listening experience. Features a variety of tweaks such as new mixing, extended intros and outtros, a few extended songs, new skits, and American boy has been added to the tracklist. - 100greenmen
A comp ahmed2.0 has described is similar to late registration in sound. Has some added production, and some scrapped/alt verses. Some tracks remain unaltered. - 100greenmen

Most songs have had entirely new instrumentals that remain faithful to the original, other songs have new production, and a handful of extended intros have been added. New electronic production and soul samples are also present. Maintains the release tracklist. - 100greenmen
Fosterlynch's remaster of graduation, includes bitter sweet poetry. Higher quality preservation of subtleties that would otherwise be quieter on streaming services. - 100greenmen

A shorter graduation comp that adds a lot of new production, some instrumentals are re-created and expanded on. Expanded samples and features are also added with new intros on a few songs, along with unique sample chops. - 100greenmen
Multiple file formats, early scraps included.
A playlist with some edits from the editor who put it together. Lots of added features and scrapped/alt verses. Includes American Boy, and Us Placers in the tracklist. – 100greenmen

The third vaporwave comp by the editor, this time remaining more faithful to the Graduation tracklist. New production and verses from various pop songs pitched down dominate the tracks in a similar fashion to his previous comps. – 100greenmen
Overhaul, Berais, Multiple file formats, alt cover.

A short comp with new instrumentals in the style of The College Dropout, and an altered tracklist to include scrapped tracks, as well as a new intro and outtro, New soul samples and beats. Also includes a Diamonds and Dollars Edit. – 100greenmen

An extension that adds intros and outtros from different versions of the songs from the glow in the dark tour, and some leaks. Lots of new features are added from other artists. The Ne-yo song Because of you is also added with an extended instrumental to make room for a verse featuring Kanye West. – 100greenmen

Based on a tracklist by Big Brother for his earth 2054 timeline where an album containing tracks from LR, and some other material Kanye produced or featured on instead of the more familiar release tracklist. Production differences vary from track to track to maintain a consistent sound that balances LR and Graduation’s styles, likely meant to be more of a continuation of LR’s style. – 100greenmen
Overhaul, Biobthe1 & co., Multiple alt covers, multiple file formats.

This comp takes scrapped songs from Late Registration, Graduation, and Common's album Be to make an entirely fabricated take on a Kanye album from this time period. Kanye's Track from the 'Voices of a grass roots movement' album produced to promote Barack Obama's 2008 Presidential run is also included. Added production on every track makes for a sound similar to Late Registration with some old-school hip-hop influence and mixing to match. - 100greenmen

This comp puts vocals from the release Graduation tracklist (and bittersweet poetry) over top new custom sample chops that loop for the duration of the tracks, with a few very minor touch ups. – 100greenmen

Up to Graduation Kanye had a plan to release 4 albums, the last of which was intended to be Good Ass Job. However after Graduation was released his mother had unexpectedly passed away and his then Fiance broke up with him. This series of events lead to such a drastic change in Kanye's life he felt compelled to interrupt work on Good Ass Job to express his grief and loneliness Work would begin in short and the resulting album Inspired by Kid Cudi's first mixtape (who was also recruited to write for the album) was released in 2008 as his fourth studio album. Some minor experiments with the eponymous 808's Synthesizer from GAJ and his practice with singing were utilized to form the sound on this album alongside heavy usage of auto-tune, all elements that were criticized at the time upon it's release. The orchestral elements from previous eras were still present, although they did little to win over fans and critics who did not like the new sound. This album would go on to inspire many other artists, most notably Drake, and begin Kanye's trend of re-inventing his sound with every new project. Comps from this era contain in part or whole the tracklist of the released album, with one exception.
A variety of minor changes such as adding and removing verses, using different versions and mixing them with the release tracks, and even using later Live from Hollywood Bowl versions. - 100greenmen
The instrumentals for this album have been re-created and given more layers of synths and bass, some vocals and orchestral instrumentals taken from Live at Hollywood Bowl. - 100greenmen
3 Bonus tracks, and an alt cover.

This comp reduces the tracklist and uses leaked tracks with a rougher vocal delivery and lighter autotune. Also adds some additional production and references making for a very different sound while remaining faithful to the work Kanye did on the album. - 100greenmen
New production is added, scrapped/alt features are added alongside kanye's regular verses. - 100greenmen

Stretching the definition of a comp, it appears this mixtape was produced with little more than Kanye’s blessing and released in 2008 under no label, therefore making distribution quite difficult. It takes various tracks released by Kanye up to 808’s and remixes them in a traditional fashion. - 100greenmen

Adds a bit of new production to some songs while others have new synths entirely, adds in new features alongside a re-ordered tracklist. Also has Find Your Love by Drake with an added Kanye feature. - 100greenmen

Re-creates different productions elements from other versions and performances of the songs off of 808's, most notably VH1 Storytellers, his second live recording album. Some songs are quite similar to release, while other songs have more drastic changes that still remain faithful. Also features minor mixing differences. - 100greenmen

An original project inspired by 808's with all new instrumentals, tracks, and vocals using early ai masking over the creators own voice. Meant to serve as a sequel with the same core ideas, emotions, and sounds of Kanye's album. - 100greenmen

A comp that adds new samples, vocal effects and harmonies to some tracks, adjusts mixing, and new production to others intermittently enhancing the mood for each one. Some of which would later be used for Jax’s Heartbreak (V2) Comp. - 100greenmen
An extension of 808's with no additional tracks. Instrumentals are extended and scrapped/alt features are added back. - 100greenmen
This comp adds new production of varying degrees alongside new skits baked into some of the tracks. The tracklist is cut down, and a few songs were delegated to bonus tracks. - 100greenmen
Another Vaporwave comp from the editor, this time simply adding production after pitch shifting vocals and extending the instrumentals for the songs chosen. – 100greenmen

A mashup of various Childish Gambino tracks with 808's. features vocals from Childish Gambino and his collaborators, pulling from released and unreleased material. Some instrumentation is also brought over from his tracks as well with adjusted mixing. - 100greenmen
808's & Heartbreak remastered for modern audio devices, with removed clipping. - 100greenmen

This comp features a re-done and reordered tracklist, alongside some new interlude tracks. New production mostly with synths on every song, and some added features to a few tracks. Heartless and Pinnochio story have been combined into a single track. - 100greenmen
This is a copy of Akimbo’s 808’s comp with a custom Mr. Brightside edit by Asmo as a bonus track. – 100greenmen

Initially formed in 2007, the rap group comprised of Lupe Fiasco, Kanye West, and Pharrell Williams produced it's first single; Us Placers in the same year. The song appeared on Kanye West's Can't Tell Me Nothing mix tape, and generated some excitement for the group's first album. Unfortunately due to busy schedules none of the artists were able to do much for it, and after putting it on hold for an extended period of time, it was unceremoniously canceled in 2013. Comps for this era feature songs from all three artists, adding features from the other members and some frequent collaborators. A total of 3 songs were ever produced with all 3 members involvement, and a handful of unfinished scraps that have leaked from 2007 to 2010, with the name God Unwilling considered for a potential album release. Although Lupe Fiasco would use the name again for his own solo projects in 2024, this era is unrelated to his work past this time period. While not considered a real era, comps under this umbrella aim to create simulacrums of what a CRS album might have sounded like. Songs and sounds are varied borrowing from each artists production style, and encompasses conscious hip-hop and energetic club bangers. A remix of Everyone Nose by N.E.R.D. produced by Kanye is also included in these comps regularly.

Songs are taken from all three artists discography with features added from each other, and some rearranged song structure. A few iconic songs from the Good Ass Job era are featured here. The released CRS songs are unaltered rips. Supposedly one of the first fleshed out CRS comps. - 100greenmen

SimpleJosh reconstructs snippets, creates new instrumentals, adds verses, reworks beats and more to make a short but high-quality CRS comp. It not only edits the few released CRS songs, but also uses new samples and known snippets to make a full length comp out of the era while still remaining accurate – aiwei

This comp takes songs and verses up to 2013 from each artist and adds more features from each other. A few samples are extended, borrowed from other songs, or emphasized with slightly altered mixing on the released tracks. – 100greenmen
A copy of simplejosh’s CRS comp with Asmo’s edit of If you want to as a bonus track – 100greenmen

Uses a good portion of GAJ songs and songs from around the era by the other members. Some edits are based on edits by other editors with further changes. The mixing seems unfinished on a few songs. Kinda like a big deal is unedited. This comp was meant to fit in with a larger timeline project that was scrapped. - 100greenmen

This scrapped comp has the most unique tracklist of any CRS comp. Many are mashups in a similar vein with unfinished mixing, possible placeholder verses and production. Apparently started and abandoned in 2024, it wasn't found until Chicken Man released it in 2026 with no clear intent to finish it. - 100greenmen

The most coveted, and infamous unreleased album from Kanye West. Previously said to have been the fourth of the college trilogy set to release after Graduation, it experienced it's first delay after Donda West's passing, and again after Kanye's interruption during Taylor Swift's 2009 VMA award acceptance speech. Production began after Graduation, and shifted focus with each delay. Available leaks that aren't just beats feature more melodic singing and some experiments with the 808's synthesizer. A myriad of themes and sounds were covered albeit many songs are noticeably unfinished missing verses, frequent use of kanye mumble, even songs that have yet to be heard. Many collaborators were brought on for features and production ideas before the project ultimately transitioned into My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy in spring of 2010. Comps of this era may share some crossover with MBDTF as many songs would still be worked on during that period of time. More frequently GAJ is envisioned either before or after the VMA's incident with the former having a more narrow scope, and the latter combining unreleased tracks with earlier versions of released tracks. There was also an album title "Winter Spring Summer Fall" which would feature songs for every season. Little is known of this particular album as the title would not be used long, some comps here attempt to re-create this idea using songs from this era.

To promote MBDTF's release, Kanye would release songs under the 'GOOD Fridays' moniker every Friday from 8/20/2010 to 12/15/2010. Although the album proper released on 11/22/2010. Some GOOD Fridays tracks have been used in GAJ comps due to their relative completion, as they had been worked on during the time the album was still considered Good Ass Job. A verse from Rhymefest's Raw Dawg mixtape was taken for an edit by Ivy & Casual, made into an intro skit, periodically included in these comps.

A comp with a mix of reworked MBDTF songs and scraps as well as a handful of GAJ songs, reenvisioning the album as a synth-pop influenced experience. Icy's added production is impressive and unique, with its reimagining of songs being especially respectable. Although mixing is questionable at times, it definitely still stands out in its overall creativity and quality. – aiwei

One of the first widespread and noteworthy GAJ comps attempting to overhaul the era. A mix of raw leaks and edited files with new samples and verses to fill empty space or replace mumble. Would also go on to inspire other influential and trivial comps. The outtakes are serviceable on their own, even if they are clearly under-cooked. - 100greenmen

Contains a mixture of tracks from 808’s & HB and GAJ with the intention of serving as a GAJ that would release instead of 808’s. Tracks have new instrumentals to fit the earliest iterations of GAJ songs with the synths 808’s & HB is famous for, a few tracks featuring drake are also included. – 100greenmen

Santino's debut comp, and while they would become an extremely influential editor its age shows in its mixing and audio quality. Despite that, the comp contains a multitude of very creative edits with added verses, production and features rounding out its tracks. It paved the way for Santino's later work in the era laying down the standard for Santino's reputation of unique tracklisting, serving as an introduction to Santino's later contributions to the GAJ era as a whole. - aiwei. Also lowkey delete ALL of my edits yo that shit needs to stay gone. - Santino

Akimbo's comp updates the mixing on the tracks while adding some additional prod to fit in with the electronic songs for the era. Some songs received more attention than others, minor trimming was also applied to songs shortening intros and outtros. Also includes added features, almost no mumble, and an emphasis on tracks with Kanye's singing. - 100greenmen

This early comp mainly uses GOOD Friday tracks and GAJ leaks without mumble from the era, with some shortened songs serving as interludes as well as a speech Kanye would give during a live performance titled "Pinocchio story 2". - 100greenmen
Loosely based on the leaked GAJ beat tape, several iconic songs from the era have had vocals removed, only keeping samples and the beats. – 100greenmen

BenDaBoi's debut comp, it focuses on re-arranging sections of songs, adding features, and in some cases mashing two versions of songs together. An interlude was cobbled together from Kanye's interruption at the VMA's and a news report about it, with the background chanting from Power. A V1 of the comp titled "Album for Will" is archived with the comp. It's mixed horribly, and uses bad extracts. I like to pretend it doesn't exist. - 100greenmen. I also like to pretend V1 doesn’t exist. - Bendaboi
A few .m4a's, alt cover, credits, compressed V1 copy.

A Good Ass Job comp sporting many GAJ classics in its tracklist, chrispo's comp aims to recreate the feelings present in the G.O.O.D. Fridays singles, reworking tracks into high-energy cuts with added production that adds to the vibe that tracks try to create and is reminiscent of early Kanye prod. With both intense and relatively mellow instrumentals under high energy verses from Kanye, chrispo's GAJ is a nice experience that adds to its successors iterations of the era while giving love to each track in unique ways. – Aiwei

Debut comp from Ghostbuster2k, he has re-arranged many samples, verses, and added his own production to many of the songs here. Mixing has been adjusted to make the songs sound more consistent, and contains some unique twists on skits. Sounds like a realistic release from Kanye from before the VMA's incident. - 100greenmen

Graybones re-creates several instrumentals with pure electronic synths and adds some to the rest of the tracks. The vocal extracts are outdated, though they are still at a listenable quality. A few features are added and some verse re-arranging has been done. - 100greenmen
Multiple file formats, instrumentals, bonus tracks.

Based on the canceled tour of the same name, a would be collaboration between Kanye West and Lady Gaga. Scrapped Lady Gaga songs from The Fame and GAJ are utilized. Gaga is added to Kanye's Tracks and vice verse, with the exception of the final track. Production in line with Gaga's electro-dance sound is added to the GAJ tracks, with some minor touch ups on tracks from The Fame. - 100greenmen

It is no exaggeration to call this the most famous and influential comp of Yedits history. Often considered definitive despite its age it was a landmark for its use of AI to reduce mumble the remade instrumentals among other prominent features. There are a litany of changes to go over, and they did everything possible to make a comp that sounds "finished" building on established conventions to give the songs within a unique identity. While some may consider it outdated by modern standards, its instrumentals and stems were used in other comps going forward, reinforcing the quality work done here. - 100greenmen
Art, bonus tracks, multiple file formats, credits.

This comp has minimal overlap with its Pastelle produced inspiration, instead focusing on more obscure and less edited pre-VMA tracks, giving them previously never-before-seen overhauls. Each song has added production, verses, beatswitches, fleshed out textures, additional sections, and more changes which all contribute to edits that feel like brand-new songs when compared to their contemporaries. It also minimizes its use of Pastelle's GAJ and its edits of popular tracks maintain their personality, with their interpretations being unique among the sea of others, such as in the comp's Flashing Lights 2 or Throw Money Everywhere. - aiwei
Art, bonus tracks, multiple file formats, credits.

Biob's second pass at a GAJ comp; mostly re-arranging and mixing different song versions together. Drums and bass are added to mimic what a GAJ comp could have looked like in early 2010. Existing samples for the era are also applied in a few spots, mixing has been altered to emphasize bass when it is present on a track. Sounds closer to an 'old-kanye' album and would fit in as a natural evolution of his style from 2007. - 100greenmen

A release ready comp, lots of added production is applied to fill out the instrumentals and a tracklist with minimal mumble is utilized. New samples chops and features are also prevelant, making for an interpretation of the GAJ era that feels realistic to Kanye's production style from Graduation. - 100greenmen

Remastered tracks that have added production, albeit lightly applied. Verses are added from other songs but otherwise quite a bit of mumble is deliberately left on for those who prefer the way leaked tracks sound, alongside their GOOD Fridays counter parts. Many older versions of GAJ tracks are used for a stripped back feel. - 100greenmen

Released alongside Simplejosh's Good ass job (V2) comp, this era accurate shitpost pitch shifts the vocals and instrumentals selectively to make a more off-putting and painful listening experience. - 100greenmen

Likely one of if not the first, of Mochi&Broccoli's comps. Featured artists verses are swapped with other Kanye verses and some remastering is done, with varying results. Some unique mashups help the comp stand out from others, but otherwise it's very indicative of comp creation from the early 2020's. - 100greenmen

High quality remade and touched up instrumentals focusing on live instruments with minimal retained synth production. Some samples are also used less frequently or removed altogether, and features are added to some songs. Feels intended to sound like what My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy would on release. - 100greenmen
A playlist from the early 2020's, made with a mix of edits and leaks, as well as R1600's custom edits. - 100greenmen

JuyTuy's first Gaj comp, many instrumentals have had a lot of small samples or new production at points to create a fuller sound for each song while remaining faithful. Also features an impressive ai de-mumble of the track See me again. Overall a realistic sound for a 2009 release of the album. – 100greenmen
1 bonus track, 3 scraps, art, and instrumentals

Frickinfire's first GAJ playlist, this one separates the tracks into two discs. No particular theme or reason is discernible other than splitting the large tracklist down for easier listening. A good way to experience a near complete list of the most GAJ edits for earlier versions of songs when fewer leaks had been discovered, with some mumble. Also includes the track Kinda like a big deal from Clipse. - 100greenmen

Sometime during early to mid 2012, Kanye had started working on his next solo album. He worked with various artists and producers to create music venting frustrations on the music industry and his life leading up to this point, heavy sexual themes, and a few love songs about his New wife Kim Kardashian.. Industrial synths, loud aggressive bass, and distorted auto-tune would be utilized alongside more traditional instrumentation to make beats that were in your face aggressive alongside more surreal and mellow songs. He would produce and enormous amount of tracks over the next several months and explore new sounds for his music. While many leaked songs from this era are unfinished or missing the ones we have access to are unable to paint a cohesive picture of what it was meant to be. This almost mythical status has given the era an air of intense mystery and speculation giving way to fans' imaginations to fill in the gaps. While some fans consider this to be a fake era, as Thank God For Drugs was never technically scrapped, it's a useful disambiguation for comps trying to imagine what it could have been. Several names were considered but TGFD has remained the most prominent. There are also a litany of interviews and material made during production to suggest the album initially took on a different direction than Yeezus would eventually take. Various instrumentals and even verses made during these sessions would also be cannibalized for other projects, most notably Travis Scott who would use multiple songs for his own future projects. As this project would eventually become Yeezus after Kanye had sought help from producer Rick Rubin to help finish it, TGFD comps often add a sound to match the mythology before Rick Ruben's involvement. This can range from more experimental sounds to using older/alt verses and takes to distinguish it from Yeezus itself. As well as the afore mentioned leaked songs.

During mid 2014 Kanye had finally begun work on a new EP with the intent of fleshing out songs and ideas left on the cutting room floor for Yeezus. This plan however was quickly superseded by the production of new material that strayed away from the Industrial sounds and into trap and yet more experimental territory. Alongside previous collaborators, he also started working with more artists, notably Paul McCartney who would lend his instrumentation and singing to be used in Kanye’s music, and Keyon Christ who would go on to work with him on several other projects. It’s not clear why the direction of the album changed so much during 2013, but the plan of using leftover material from Yeezus must have dissolved sometime before 2014 as the project would eventually be re-named So Help Me God during mid 2015. Several songs for some G.O.O.D. Music signees were produced by Ye and released during this era, while many while the rest would continue production after the project changed direction or dropped entirely. A few songs like FML, Wolves, and 3500 (thirty-five hunna) originated here and would undergo drastic transformations according to the artists involved and scant leaks related to these early versions, so typically comps for this era will incorporate the later versions as it’s all we have available. Comps for this era are also prone to containing mumble or no verse at all, if more complete versions exist they simply have not leaked and it’s dubious if they will going forward. If these or other collaborations yet to be heard from ever leaked it would dramatically alter the perception of this era. A notoriously challenging era to edit as standards have risen over the years and older comps have aged.

As the Yeezus 2 sessions progressed the aim of the project changed and resembled little of what it set out to be. Tracks began to drift away from the experimental production and narrowed down into trap and more typical hip-hop styles, new songs were recorded for this era and in early 2015 it was announced as the next upcoming album by Kanye. A few singles would release before the reveal, and one during march likely showing off the intent to release it, but ultimately late spring Kanye would announce a name change to swish and many tracks would be dropped in favor of yet a new change in direction. SHMG remains an enigmatic footnote in public perception due to the released singles that clearly resembled an album rollout, and it is unknown why it was canceled. Comps for this era can be a mix of tracks from Y2 all the way to The Life of Pablo as an absurd amount of tracks had been worked on during this era and it shared many of the same collaborators as Y2 and Swish. Many tracks remain buried, but enough has leaked to give a wide variety of sounds and moods that an editor could feasibly draw upon to match their vision. An accurate SMGH re-creation is in the eye of the beholder as leaked tracklists do indicate something of a plan, typically either leaning into the trap genre or the more sentimental or synth heavy side. Despite being a transitional period between Y2 and Tlop, there’s still a unique quality to the early versions of tracks and songs that would be dropped during this era.

This sheet aims to define terminology used for yedits comps and music that might not be common to hear outside of dedicated communities.
Vanilla comps add quality of life changes, and minor additions to remain faithful.

Editor is a term for someone editing music. This can range from simple things like extending a songs beat, adding new production elements, or more intense work like re-creating beats, making new beats entirely, or using AI models, sometimes custom trained ones to add new lyrics where none existed before.
Overhauls make a given album sound different from the source material, while still retaining it's sonic identity.

The standard term for a song that has been edited. This can encompass anything from a minor tweak, added verses, mixing, added production, and so on. Typically they're broken down into different categories depending on what has been changed. Anything from vanilla, to reworking a given song entirely. Some leaked or unfinished songs are only given touch ups to 'complete' them for example, while others are more akin to remixes.
Renovations remain within the spirit of a given era, but makes changes or adds new sounds.

A de-mumble is a process of reducing the amount of mumbling in a song. Typically this means cutting out small or large portions of audio where the spoken lyrics are inaudible or indiscernible. The goal is making a song more cohesive and still fit the beat. Some editors will take the vocal track of a song containing heavy mumble and de-mumble it to the best of their ability for others to use.
Remixes take the source material and make something entirely new out of it until it's unrecognizeable.

Comp is a catch-all term for community made album. Typically it can encompass a wide range of things, but usually refers to albums made up of released, or leaked songs edited to suit the editors personal taste. Playlists are lumped in with comps at times.
Shitposts can embody elements from all the other types of comp, with the goal of being humorous, and low effort.

Playlists are sometimes conflated with comps, but there are some key differences. Playlists are typically made of up different edits whether they are from a comp or not to create a curated listening experience. The goal is usually to edit within the same era to make the users ideal version of an album, but some take it further and dedicate their efforts to making curated experiences for others, even adding their own custom edits or further editing other editors edits. It’s not uncommon for released or leaked songs to be included as well.
Remasters aim to bring the mix of a given comps audio up to the standards of modern audio devices.

A stem is a track with an individual instrument, sound, someone's spoken lyrics, and nothing else. These are used all across music creation to make mixing easier and better organize the elements of any given song while it's being made. Editors sometimes include stems with their comps so other people can mix the songs however they like, or use them in making their own edits. Lossless formats are usually preferred for this.

Extracts are specific parts of a song like the vocals, one or multiple sounds from the beat, and so on taken from a song to be used like a stem for other songs. The process of extracting any element from a song with any tool or program is typically very tedious and can yield tinny audio or audio that retains a quiet echo of other parts of the song it was taken from without proper care.

Big Brother's alternate universe timeline: Earth 2054. Detailing a life that lead to the release of some unreleased albums, as well as altered versions of his released discography, although newer versions of the living document have been continually worked on and passed onto a new team. Many individuals or folks dedicated to making playlists to match the tracklists made for this AU have their own takes on it or will make new comps to suit it.

Some people who are especially invested in Ye's history or the mythology behind his released and unreleased albums create alternate universe timelines to suit a narrative justifying the release, and cancellation of certain albums. These can be accompanied by playlists or comps created by other editors and the author of the AU themselves, but the two are not mutually exclusive.

And LP refers to Kanye’s solo album releases under his Name and/or label with unreleased albums scrapped before a release grouped under that LP. For example The College Dropout is LP1, Graduation is LP3, Yeezus is LP6, with the final agreed upon LP being LP10; Donda. After that album it gets messy as Kanye’s production cycles would get more messy and complex resulting in situations where Donda 2 released on the stem player, and an updated version would release in 2025 after both vultures albums. Bully would be teased after Vultures 2 but before cuck was being worked on/leaked, then after cuck was scrapped and Bully V2 was released you could categorize those, but a common community census has yet to emerge.
